brief: Writes a score as notation and as a MIDI file, and says what each format could not carry.
detail: Notation is a rendering of the score and never its source: ABC 2.1 text, MusicXML and a Standard MIDI File, type 1, are written from the same stzSoundScore. Quarter tones are written in each format's own terms, ^/ and _/ in ABC and decimal alterations in MusicXML; a pitch further than 5 cents from the nearest quarter tone, and a duration rounded by more than a hundredth of a beat, are counted in Losses. MIDI has no quarter tones, so every pitched note gets a pitch bend on a channel of its own, and strokes go to the drum channel. Everything is text or bytes: no audio device is opened and nothing is played. The files have not been heard or read by a musician (UNPERCEIVED): they are checked by their bytes and text.
receiver:
oS = StzSoundScoreOfQ("C4 D4 E4 C4")
oS.Tempo(90)
o1 = StzSoundNotationQ(oS)
example: ? StzFindFirst("C4 D4 E4 C4", o1.ToABC("Tiny study")) > 0
